meta.title: Utility hardship mapping - Western Australia
meta.how_it_works: Signals (seen in account data or asked of the customer) point to circumstances; circumstances point to solutions. Each record also lists its links in the other direction (signals.points_to, solutions.used_for).

scoring.flag_when: at least 1 strong signal, OR at least 2 supporting signals
scoring.sensitive_rule: Circumstances with sensitivity 'sensitive' or 'safety' need at least 1 strong signal; supporting signals alone never flag them.
scoring.strong: Enough on its own to suggest the circumstance (usually a direct customer answer or an unambiguous account event).
scoring.supporting: Only meaningful in combination with other signals.
scoring.safety_rule: Circumstances with sensitivity 'safety' are never actioned automatically; they create a task for trained staff.

guardrails: Flags trigger an offer of help, never a penalty. Do not use them in credit, collections escalation or disconnection decisions.
Sensitive circumstances (health, addiction, bereavement, separation, housing status) come from what the customer tells you, with consent. Do not infer them from usage or payment data.
Safety circumstances (family violence, economic abuse, elder abuse): no automated contact. Route to trained staff, protect address and account details, and avoid asking for proof.
Keep a person in the loop: show staff which signals raised each flag so they can check it makes sense before acting.
Health information is 'sensitive information' under the Australian Privacy Principles and needs consent to collect. Collect only what is needed to help.
Program amounts and rules change, often on 1 July. Re-check every solution marked 'Not re-checked' before launch and all of them each year.
Measure outcomes, not flags: did the customer actually get connected to the help?

circumstance_types.name: Life situation
circumstance_types.meaning: Something happening in the customer's life.
circumstance_types.who_acts: Offer support, payment help and referrals.

circumstance_types.name: Access barrier
circumstance_types.meaning: Something that makes it hard to get or use help.
circumstance_types.who_acts: Change how you communicate or who you talk to.

circumstance_types.name: Bill or account issue
circumstance_types.meaning: A problem with the bill, meter, payment or account itself.
circumstance_types.who_acts: Fix the account, then check whether help is still needed.

circumstance_types.name: Company practice
circumstance_types.meaning: Something the provider is doing, or failing to do.
circumstance_types.who_acts: Fix the process internally, and put this customer right.

circumstance_types.name: Knock-on effect
circumstance_types.meaning: Harm that follows when other problems go unaddressed.
circumstance_types.who_acts: Treat as urgent and act the same day.

signals.name: Usage spike

signals.example_rule: usage vs same period last year > +40%

signals.name: Water never stops flowing

signals.name: Very low or falling usage

signals.name: Concession lapsed

signals.name: Concession card on file
signals.detect: A concession card is linked to the account (eligibility indicator).

signals.name: No concession linked
signals.detect: No concession on account although other data suggests eligibility.
signals.example_rule: no concession AND (eligibility hint from answers or notes)

signals.name: Repeat contact
signals.detect: Customer keeps contacting about the same bill or issue.

signals.name: Complaint or ombudsman referral
signals.detect: Formal complaint logged, or ombudsman has referred the case.

signals.name: Life events mentioned in contact notes

signals.name: Extreme heat forecast
signals.detect: Bureau of Meteorology forecast maximum of 38°C or more (42°C north of the 26th parallel) at the customer's nearest forecast town in the next 7 days.

signals.name: Extreme fire danger forecast
signals.detect: Bureau of Meteorology fire danger rating of Extreme or Catastrophic in the customer's forecast district (the free forecast usually rates tomorrow only).

signals.name: Weather warning for the area
signals.detect: An active Bureau of Meteorology warning (heatwave, severe weather, fire weather, cyclone or flood) for the customer's forecast district.

signals.name: Lives in a disadvantaged area
signals.detect: The customer's postcode is among the most disadvantaged 20% in WA (ABS SEIFA 2021, Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage, WA decile 1 or 2). It describes the area, not the person, so it never counts towards flagging a circumstance; it adds priority points once the customer's own evidence has flagged one.

solutions.name: Payment extension
solutions.how_to_access: Offer extra time on this bill. Grant it if the customer asks before the due date and has no other extension or arrangement in place, and record the new due date on the account.
solutions.key_facts: Extra time to pay one bill. Synergy's rule: available if requested before the due date and no other extension or arrangement is in place.

solutions.name: Interest- and fee-free payment arrangement
solutions.provider: Us: customer service or hardship team
solutions.how_to_access: Agree a plan the customer can afford, based on their capacity to pay. Spread the bill and any arrears into smaller amounts and record the plan on the account.
solutions.contact: Customer service; hardship team for larger or repeat arrears
solutions.key_facts: The customer pays the bill and arrears in smaller amounts over time, with no interest or fees (Synergy describes its plans this way). Telcos must offer this as one of their hardship options.

solutions.name: Our hardship program
solutions.how_to_access: Offer a hardship assessment and transfer the customer to the hardship team.
solutions.contact: Hardship team (internal transfer). Reference: Synergy 13 13 53 | Horizon Power 1800 267 926
solutions.key_facts: Electricity and gas retailers must have a hardship policy under WA rules. Synergy's Keeping Connected program, for example, gives a dedicated case manager, flexible terms and incentives for meeting payment goals.

solutions.name: Water Corporation hardship programs
solutions.how_to_access: For water debts, refer the customer to Water Corporation, directly or through a financial counsellor.
solutions.key_facts: Water Corporation's programs include Water Assist (an interest-free plan where Water Corporation matches payments), Time Assist and Start Over (now open to debts over $2,000), plus flexible plans and extensions.

solutions.name: Water Corporation Medical Assist (home dialysis)
solutions.how_to_access: Tell the customer the allowance is automatic once WA Home Therapies sends Water Corporation their details. There is nothing to apply for.
solutions.key_facts: Free water allowance of up to 30,000 litres for households doing home dialysis.

solutions.name: Hardship Utility Grant Scheme (HUGS)
solutions.provider: WA Government (Department of Communities). We assess and refer.
solutions.how_to_access: Once payment arrangements and other hardship options are exhausted, assess the customer for HUGS and refer them to the HUGS Service Centre.
solutions.contact: Our hardship team makes the referral; HUGS Service Centre hugs@communities.wa.gov.au
solutions.key_facts: Covers up to 85% of the outstanding amount; caps apply and are higher north of the 26th parallel. The HUGS assessment can include referrals to financial counselling, legal advocacy and Foodbank.

solutions.name: Energy Assistance Payment (EAP)
solutions.provider: WA Government; the credit is applied by Synergy or Horizon Power
solutions.how_to_access: Register the customer's eligible concession card on the account so the annual credit is applied. If we're not Synergy or Horizon Power, refer them to ECES instead.
solutions.contact: Customer service. Reference: Synergy 13 13 53 | Horizon Power 1800 267 926
solutions.key_facts: Annual bill credit for holders of means-tested Commonwealth concession cards. Customers of other retailers use ECES instead.

solutions.name: Dependent Child Rebate
solutions.provider: WA Government; applied by the retailer, or through RevenueWA (ECES)
solutions.how_to_access: If the customer gets the EAP and has dependent children, add the rebate to the account, or point them to ECES if we can't apply it.
solutions.contact: Customer service. Reference: Synergy 13 13 53 | Horizon Power 1800 267 926 | RevenueWA
solutions.key_facts: Extra rebate for EAP recipients with dependent children.

solutions.name: Air Conditioning Rebate
solutions.provider: WA Government; applied by the retailer, or through RevenueWA (ECES)
solutions.how_to_access: Check the criteria first, then apply the rebate for an eligible EAP recipient or refer them to RevenueWA.
solutions.contact: Customer service. Reference: Horizon Power 1800 267 926 | RevenueWA
solutions.key_facts: Available in certain cases to EAP recipients. Check the criteria before offering it.

solutions.name: Energy Concession Extension Scheme (ECES)
solutions.how_to_access: If we can't apply the EAP directly (for example an embedded network or another retailer), refer the customer to apply online through RevenueWA.
solutions.key_facts: For eligible concession card holders who can't get the EAP from their supplier. The EAP rate is $377.14 a year from 1 July 2026. Not available where a landlord forwards the bill or rent is all-inclusive.

solutions.name: Life Support Equipment Energy Subsidy (LSEES)
solutions.how_to_access: Tell the customer about the subsidy and refer them to apply through the RevenueWA online portal with medical certification. Register them as a life support customer too.
solutions.key_facts: Annual subsidy for each item of specified life support equipment used at home on specialist medical advice.

solutions.name: Register the customer for life support
solutions.how_to_access: Add life support registration to the account straight away when the customer or their carer tells us about the equipment. Follow up for medical confirmation.
solutions.contact: Customer service. Reference: Synergy 13 13 53 | Horizon Power 1800 267 926
solutions.key_facts: The WA Government advises anyone using life support equipment to register with their retailer as soon as possible. Do this before anything else.

solutions.name: Thermoregulatory Dysfunction Energy Subsidy (TDES)
solutions.how_to_access: Tell the customer about the subsidy and refer them to apply through the RevenueWA online portal with specialist medical advice.
solutions.key_facts: $832 a year, paid in advance, for means-tested concession card holders (or their dependants) who need heating or cooling because of a qualifying condition.

solutions.name: Pensioner and seniors water service charge rebate
solutions.how_to_access: For an owner-occupier with an eligible card, refer them to apply to Water Corporation, which notifies their council.
solutions.key_facts: Rebate or deferral on water service charges for owner-occupiers holding a Pensioner Concession Card, State Concession Card or WA Seniors Card.

solutions.name: Water Corporation leak allowance
solutions.how_to_access: Tell the customer to repair the leak, then apply online within six months of the repair.
solutions.key_facts: Covers up to 50% of the estimated water lost through an undetected leak.

solutions.name: Bill review, meter test or special read
solutions.provider: Us: customer service or billing team
solutions.how_to_access: Review the bill and, if it still looks wrong, arrange a special meter read or meter test. Tell the customer what you find.
solutions.key_facts: Our first step for a suspected error, before it goes to an ombudsman.

solutions.name: Energy and Water Ombudsman WA
solutions.provider: External: Energy and Water Ombudsman Western Australia
solutions.how_to_access: Try to resolve the complaint first. If we can't, tell the customer they can lodge a complaint online or by phone, as we must.
solutions.key_facts: Free, independent complaint resolution for electricity, gas and water customers.

solutions.name: Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman
solutions.how_to_access: Try to resolve the complaint first. If we can't, tell the customer they can lodge it with the TIO online or by phone.
solutions.key_facts: Free complaint resolution for phone and internet problems, including bills and disconnections.

solutions.name: Telco hardship protections
solutions.provider: Us: hardship team (telco services; regulated by ACMA)
solutions.how_to_access: Offer financial hardship assistance and record which options the customer chose.
solutions.key_facts: Telcos must proactively identify customers who may be in hardship, offer at least six assistance options, take reasonable steps to keep services connected, and not sell a debt while a hardship arrangement is active.

solutions.name: Family violence protections
solutions.provider: Us: family violence or hardship team (electricity and gas retailers are regulated by the ERA)
solutions.how_to_access: Apply our family violence policy. Don't ask the customer to retell their story, protect their account and contact details from anyone else on the account, and consider their situation before any disconnection.
solutions.contact: Family violence or hardship team (internal transfer)
solutions.key_facts: Electricity and gas retailers must have a family violence policy covering staff training, protecting account information from third parties, not making customers repeat their disclosure, and considering circumstances before disconnection. Water and telco providers: follow your own policy.

solutions.name: Family and domestic violence helplines
solutions.how_to_access: Offer the helpline numbers only when it is safe to do so. They answer 24 hours.
solutions.contact: Give the customer: Women's DV Helpline 1800 007 339 | Men's DV Helpline 1800 000 599 | 1800RESPECT 1800 737 732 | Emergency 000
solutions.key_facts: Crisis support, safety planning and refuge referrals.

solutions.name: Escaping Violence Payment
solutions.how_to_access: Mention the payment and give the number so the customer can check whether they're eligible.
solutions.key_facts: For people 18 or over who have recently experienced intimate partner violence, have a changed living situation and are under financial stress.

solutions.name: Free financial counselling
solutions.provider: External: National Debt Helpline (run by Vinnies in WA) / Financial Counsellors' Association of WA
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer for free financial counselling. Give them the number, or point them to fcawa.org to find a local counsellor.
solutions.key_facts: Free, independent counsellors who look at the customer's whole situation, negotiate with creditors (including us) and refer to legal, food and other support. Water Corporation hardship programs often need an assessment from a registered financial counsellor.

solutions.name: Free interpreter (TIS National)
solutions.provider: External: Translating and Interpreting Service (Australian Government)
solutions.how_to_access: Call TIS National, ask for the customer's language and bring the interpreter into the call. Note the language on the account.
solutions.key_facts: Free phone interpreting so the customer can talk to us in their language.

solutions.name: National Relay Service
solutions.how_to_access: Accept calls through the National Relay Service and tell the customer it's available. Note their preferred contact method on the account.
solutions.key_facts: Phone access for people who are deaf or have hearing or speech difficulties.

solutions.name: Authorised representative or alternative contact
solutions.how_to_access: With the customer's consent, add an authorised representative (financial counsellor, carer or family member) or change how we contact them. Check for signs of financial abuse before adding anyone.
solutions.key_facts: Lets someone the customer trusts help, and gets bills and notices to the customer in a form they can use.

solutions.name: Change account holder and review who owes the debt
solutions.how_to_access: Move the account into the right name and review who should owe the debt.
solutions.key_facts: Helps after a separation, when a housemate leaves, or when debt was put in someone's name without their agreement.

solutions.name: Deceased account and bereavement support
solutions.how_to_access: Follow our bereavement process: close or transfer the account and pause collection while the estate is sorted out.
solutions.key_facts: Pausing collection takes pressure off the family while the estate is being dealt with.

solutions.name: Energy or water efficiency help
solutions.how_to_access: Give usage advice, or arrange a meter audit (or a water audit for water customers).
solutions.key_facts: Synergy's hardship policy includes meter audits and help to reduce use; Water Corporation considers a water audit for high-use hardship customers.

solutions.name: Plan or tariff review
solutions.how_to_access: Compare the customer's current plan or tariff with our alternatives for their usage, and move them if another one is cheaper.
solutions.key_facts: Residential gas and telco customers can switch providers; most WA households can't switch electricity retailer but may be able to change tariff.

solutions.name: Link concession card to account
solutions.how_to_access: Check whether the customer has a concession card and link it to the account. Remind them to register it with their other providers too.
solutions.key_facts: Many WA concessions only apply once the card is linked to the account.

solutions.name: Centrepay
solutions.provider: External: Services Australia (we must accept Centrepay)
solutions.how_to_access: If we accept Centrepay, help the customer set up regular deductions from their Centrelink payments to us.
solutions.contact: Services Australia; customer service sets up the account side
solutions.key_facts: Bills are paid automatically on payment day, which suits customers paid fortnightly.

solutions.name: Smaller regular payments or paying in advance
solutions.how_to_access: Set up weekly or fortnightly payments, or let the customer pay in advance.
solutions.key_facts: Spreads big seasonal bills across the year. Synergy accepts payments in advance at no cost.

solutions.name: Fee waiver
solutions.how_to_access: Waive late, dishonour or reconnection fees for a customer having payment problems or affected by family violence.
solutions.key_facts: The WA electricity code includes a fee waiver for customers experiencing payment problems or affected by family violence. Other utilities: follow your own policy.

solutions.name: Pause disconnection and reconnect
solutions.provider: Us: customer service or credit team
solutions.how_to_access: Hold any disconnection while the customer's hardship is assessed, or reconnect them if they've been cut off.
solutions.key_facts: WA codes limit disconnection (for example, gas can't be disconnected for a residential debt under $300). The ombudsman can step in if we didn't follow the process.

solutions.name: Emergency relief and food support
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer to a financial counsellor or a local community service for food or emergency relief.
solutions.contact: Give the customer: National Debt Helpline 1800 007 007 (can refer)
solutions.key_facts: Food parcels, vouchers and one-off help. HUGS assessments can include a Foodbank referral.

solutions.name: No-interest loan for essential items
solutions.provider: External: Anglicare WA and other no-interest loan providers
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer to apply for a no-interest loan to replace an inefficient appliance or cover an essential cost.
solutions.key_facts: Helps replace an inefficient fridge, heater or hot water system, or cover an essential cost, without interest.

solutions.name: Free legal help with debt and credit
solutions.provider: External: Legal Aid WA / community legal centres
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer for free legal advice.
solutions.key_facts: Advice on debts, defaults, bankruptcy, estates and economic abuse.

solutions.name: Consumer Protection WA
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer by phone or online.
solutions.key_facts: Help with scams, rental issues (landlord and tenant responsibilities) and unfair sales practices.

solutions.name: Identity theft support (IDCARE)
solutions.how_to_access: Secure the account, then refer the customer to IDCARE for a response plan.
solutions.key_facts: Free help to respond when someone's identity has been misused.

solutions.name: Disaster relief
solutions.how_to_access: Offer our disaster relief (bill deferral or a payment plan) and point the customer to any government disaster payments.
solutions.key_facts: Bill deferrals and payment plans from us, plus any government disaster payments that apply.

solutions.name: Mental health and crisis support
solutions.how_to_access: Offer the number if the customer is distressed. Lifeline's staff are trained to respond to distress.
solutions.key_facts: 24-hour crisis support.

solutions.name: Gambling Help
solutions.how_to_access: Offer the number, by phone or online, 24 hours.
solutions.key_facts: Free, confidential counselling for people affected by gambling, including family members.

solutions.name: Carer Gateway
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer by phone or online.
solutions.key_facts: Support, respite and counselling for carers.

solutions.name: Check government payment entitlements
solutions.how_to_access: Suggest the customer checks with Centrelink or a financial counsellor that they're getting everything they're entitled to.
solutions.key_facts: Resolves delayed or stopped payments and checks for payments the household may be missing.

solutions.name: Prepayment meter hardship assistance
solutions.provider: Us: hardship team (Horizon Power for prepayment customers in its area)
solutions.how_to_access: Offer prepayment hardship support. If the customer is a Horizon Power prepayment customer, refer them there.
solutions.key_facts: Horizon Power's hardship information includes specific assistance for prepayment meter customers.

solutions.name: Proactive, trained outreach
solutions.provider: Us: hardship or financial care team
solutions.how_to_access: Contact the customer through a safe channel and offer help before the debt grows.
solutions.key_facts: Water Corporation uses data analytics to contact customers who may be in hardship; telcos must proactively identify them under the hardship standard.

solutions.name: Move-in and move-out help
solutions.how_to_access: Check the move-in and final readings, connection fees and the ID we accept.
solutions.key_facts: Avoids overlapping bills and the customer paying for a previous occupant's use.

solutions.name: Fair Work Ombudsman
solutions.how_to_access: Refer the customer online or by phone for help with unpaid wages.
solutions.key_facts: Help recovering unpaid wages.
